In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a single measure of treatment adherence is not recommended.
the use of antihypertensive medication is a necessary and effective treatment for hypertension.

the most important factors in adherence to antihypertensive treatment are patient characteristics, including patient education, knowledge, and motivation; the characteristics of the physician-patient interaction and the physician-patient relationship; and the characteristics of the medication, such as side effects and regimen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the results of our research suggest that the use of a single measure of treatment adherence, such as the Morisky Medication Adherence Scale (MMAS), may not be adequate for the assessment of hypertensive individuals' adherence to both treatment and lifestyle change.
the most effective approach to the assessment of adherence in hypertensive individuals is a combination of self-reported measures and objective measures of adherence.
the most important factor in the development of hypertension is a genetic predisposition.

adherence is a complex construct that is difficult to assess.
